reply.title: Squashing Values with a Sigmoid Curve
reply.story: When modeling probabilities or neural networks, we often need to take any number from negative infinity to positive infinity and squash it into a strict range between zero and one. A linear scale cannot do this because it grows without bound. By passing our input through an exponential growth ratio, we create a smooth S-shaped curve that compresses extreme values while leaving inputs near zero flexible. Adjusting the steepness parameter alters how quickly the transition happens, letting us control the sensitivity of the response.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the sigmoid function maps any real input into an output strictly between $0$ and $1$. Adjust the steepness to see how the transition sharpens or flattens.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness slider to change how fast the curve transitions from zero to one. Observe the output value update at the fixed marker position.
